overall:
Every DONE-WHEN heading is present. The register is carried verbatim into §2 (diffed: identical), and the thirty refuter verdicts map to traceable amendments KS-F1..F20. The document is still not ready to hand to the owner, for six reasons.

(1) The owner summary and §11 say that "accept all defaults" runs the audit and stops unless it says go. §10 KS-0 and D2 say only a counted-repeat total of zero stops the track, and KS-1's Entry has no go gate. So the defaults actually start about four build sessions, three of them Opus-implemented.

(2) §0, §9 and §12.5 were not fully updated after the refuters:
- §9 still cites the withdrawn X-05 F20 ("almost no explicit repeats").
- §9's "about 1k tokens per quiet phase" contradicts §7.7's restated cost model.
- The tally says 23 narrowed and 6 refuted, but the table and the verdicts show 21 and 8.
- §7.6 says "about 170 words"; the text is 264.

(3) §10 leaves designed mechanisms with no phase: `ks outcome`, `ks anchor`, `ks close`, revise/supersede/withdraw/accept-handle, `rescrub`, probe-in-lookup, the near-duplicate and negative-corpus write checks, and lookup-event compaction. Also, record-before-merge (§7.3) contradicts the write gate that refuses non-mainline shas.

(4) HANDOFF §6's seven defect shapes have no disposition in §8. They are miscounted as "negative results": lane R-01a classed them `other`, with no failed approaches recorded. HANDOFF §6 item 2 presents ex6's deliberate correct-PIN lock as "tests pinned the broken behaviour", and the corrections list misses it.

(5) Several interactions with the ship program are unaddressed:
- Root `eslint .` and `prettier --check .` in ci.yml's frontend job will police `tools/ks/`.
- CLAUDE.md's own honesty rule forces an edit to its CI row at KS-1.
- KS-6 and D9 pin postgres:16-alpine; the ship plan moves to 17 at P3a.
- KS sessions share the account's Opus usage with P0a–P4c; the panel already lost judges to a usage limit.
- §7.2 dispatches cheap agents to apply fixes in areas the ship plan's Routing reserves to Opus.

(6) The branch is based on main (a31924a). On that base SHIP-PLAN, G2, HARNESS-REVIEW, OWNER-VIEW, w2/* and ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN do not exist; they live on docs/orchestration-design-2026-10.

None of this changes the architecture. All of it is text or scope repair.

missing.what: The local commit lease is never specified. contradictions.a: §11 'The one ruling': with all defaults 'the track runs KS-0 and stops there unless the audit says go'. §0: 'Everything else waits on its answer.'
contradictions.b: §10 KS-0 Done when and D2: 'Only a counted-repeat total of zero stops the track here; … the kill decision belongs to KS-5 and KS-9'. KS-1 Entry is just 'KS-0 done; D3 and D4 ruled'.
contradictions.resolution: Either add an explicit owner go after KS-0 to KS-1's Entry (with a nonzero D2 threshold), or rewrite §0 and §11: 'the audit sets a prior; unless it finds zero, the track builds to the pilot (about 6 sessions) and the pilot is the real stop point'.

contradictions.a: §9 'What the evidence does not establish': '48 fix-prefixed commits with almost no explicit repeats (X-05 F20)'.
contradictions.b: §0 (at least five same-cause repeats) and §12.5: 'X-05 F20's "almost no explicit repeats" is withdrawn'.
contradictions.resolution: Replace the §9 bullet with KS-C10's narrowed claim: repeats exist (3–5 by lens), and it is unproven that a store beats `git log --grep` and CLAUDE.md on them.

contradictions.a: §9 'What it costs per phase': 'about 1k tokens in a phase with no hard problem; 10–15k in a phase that records'.
contradictions.b: §7.7, restated after KS-C9: the dominant term is the round trip re-reading the caller's context as cache reads (63k+ per subagent call, hundreds of thousands in the main session), so a quiet phase pays two turns, 'not zero'.
contradictions.resolution: Delete §9's numbers and point to §7.7's formula. Give the quiet-phase cost as turns plus cache-read tokens.

contradictions.a: §7.3 and §7.6: record 'before the PR is marked ready'; the reviewer names 'its control-pair result at the PR head SHA'.
contradictions.b: §3.2: `fix_commit` must be 'a full 40-hex mainline sha'. §3.4: controls are 'mainline commits'. §7.3's write gate: 'a branch-only sha is refused with the squash commit suggested'. The squash commit does not exist before merge.
contradictions.resolution: Allow `ks record` with branch shas as state `pending_anchor` (candidate-only). Run `ks anchor` (patch-id match to the squash commit) automatically in `ks close`, and add it to §7.1, §7.6 and a KS phase.

contradictions.a: §4.1 step 3: 'the query tokenised in the temp schema of a read-only connection so a lookup never takes the write lock'.
contradictions.b: §3.6 and §3.1: every lookup writes a `lookup` event journal-first, with the index append under BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Probe-in-lookup writes a recorded gate run. §7.1 gives lookup exit 4 `store_busy`.
contradictions.resolution: Say the ranking query runs read-only and the lookup event is appended afterwards under the write lock (busy is then possible). Or make lookup events host-local, not journaled.

contradictions.a: §3.1: the journal is 'committed in batches at phase close under a local commit lease'.
contradictions.b: The same cell: 'pushed immediately after every ks record and curated approval (KS-F15)'. A push needs a commit.
contradictions.resolution: State that `ks record` and approvals commit pending events and push, and that mechanical events are batched at `ks close`.

contradictions.a: §3.1: 'a compaction or rollup of lookup events is scheduled before the journal passes about 20,000 events (KS-F6)'.
contradictions.b: §1.5 History ('never deleted'), §3.1 ('append-only, immutable'), and the §9 never-do list ('never edit, rename or delete journal files; never … prune').
contradictions.resolution: Design it: lookup events go to a separate host-local log, or a rollup event plus a new epoch directory, with old files kept. Or drop the compaction claim and raise the freshness bound.

contradictions.a: §4.2: thresholds 'Calibrated in KS-2 by leave-one-handle-out over the seed and frozen before the pilot'.
contradictions.b: The seed exists only from KS-4. KS-2 uses 'a synthetic 30-entry corpus'. §8 says each KS-4 batch recalibrates. KS-5 Deliverables include 'the thresholds as config.set events'.
contradictions.resolution: Calibrate on the KS-4 seed, freeze with a `config.set` event as a KS-4 done-when, and forbid KS-5 from changing θ (otherwise the pilot grades itself).

contradictions.a: §10 rules: 'synthetic fixtures only (real samples stay in the store home)'.
contradictions.b: §4.1 and KS-2 Scope: golden fixtures 'from the repository's own real traps'.
contradictions.resolution: Golden fixtures in `tools/ks` are scrubbed or synthetic reconstructions of real traps. Raw originals stay in the store home.

contradictions.a: §8 rule 2 and 'Order of work': the four CLAUDE.md traps are recorded in KS-4, and each KS-4 batch ends with a leave-one-handle-out replay.
contradictions.b: KS-4 Scope and Done when cover only the eight examples, the skill and the docs PR, with no traps and no replay.
contradictions.resolution: Add the trap entries (including a disposition for the 'expo export bundles JS only' trap) and the replay to the KS-4 Scope and Done when.

contradictions.a: §9: 'That a Haiku- or Sonnet-class agent benefits from a gated hit … the pilot measures with and without.'
contradictions.b: KS-5 Scope measures retrieval only (P@1, recall, acted false positives) against the grep and `git log` arms. No arm compares an agent's task outcome with and without the store.
contradictions.resolution: Add a small with/without task arm to KS-5 (same symptoms, a cheap agent with and without `ks`, outcome measured mechanically), or delete the §9 claim and move the question to KS-9.

contradictions.a: KS-R7 and §7.3: the store 'links to, never restates' the PR body's 'Decisions / ruled out' journal.

owner_readability: Accepting all defaults does not stop the track after the audit. Under D2 only zero counted repeats stops it, so the defaults start about four build sessions, three of them Opus-implemented, before the pilot can say stop. §0's 'Everything else waits on its answer' and §11's 'stops there unless the audit says go' both read as the opposite.

§0 gives no build cost. The owner sees 'one command' and 'fifteen minutes' and will not know the track is about 6 sessions to the go/stop point plus 4 after a go, much of it Opus, competing with P0a–P4c for the same usage limits.

'Nothing to run' and 'the owner does nothing per phase' hide the owner's real touchpoints: a verdict at KS-5 and at KS-9, starting Docker Desktop for KS-6, merging the docs-corrections PR and the plan amendment, and SSH at KS-8. A one-line list in §0 would prevent surprise asks.

Rule 5 reads as 'nothing leaves my machines'. Everything the store shows an agent goes to Anthropic (D7 is starred but not explained in §0), names and addresses cannot be scrubbed, and the KS-0/KS-5 evidence tables are committed to the GitHub repository.

Rule 2 reads as 'a verified hit is a proven diagnosis'. The check proves a condition is present, not that it caused this failure. For most code defects no lead is possible until the Docker checks, which are built only after the pilot. The realistic early value is config and build traps (ex7, ex8, migration traps), and §0 never says so.
'Free audit' means no code and no install. It still costs a Sonnet session plus an Opus refuter pass.
'candidate', 'lead', 'journal' and 'footprint' are used in §0 and its diagram without a one-line definition.

§0 is about 540 words plus a 13-node diagram, roughly 1.5–2 printed pages, not one. The diagram shows the journal written after the reviewer's refutation, while the design writes it first and marks the entry provisional. It also does not show what the owner does.
The ask is 'decide now' while the ship plan's next session is the owner's P0a. Say that D1 can be answered any time, that KS-0 needs nothing more from the owner, and that it should not displace P0a.
'Seventeen decisions … four genuinely yours' invites reading §11 now. Only D1 is needed now, and D7 before KS-2; say that and stop.
